name: Amazon Web Services (AWS)
quote: Amazon Web Services offers reliable, scalable, and inexpensive cloud computing services.
identity_why: identity_note: present ['amazon','web','aws'], missing [] - the page's own title is 'Cloud Computing Services - Amazon Web Services (AWS)', so identifies() passes on the full name, not on the word 'amazon' alone. This is the sub-site the earlier audit was looking for when it rejected aboutamazon.eu as the parent.
sells_why: Title and description are cloud computing services; the site is the AWS product catalogue (Products, Solutions, Pricing, re:Invent), matching 'Cloud computing platform'. data/conference_intake/staged/nacm-2026.json and naswa-summit-2025.json independently list this exhibitor at https://aws.amazon.com/.

name: Baseline Telematics
quote: Baseline Telematics Inc. (for Canadian Customers) is subject to the regulatory enforcement powers of the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada.
identity_why: identity_note on the homepage says present ['baseline'], missing ['telematics'] - the company now brands itself 'Baseline'. The full legal name appears six times in this site's own privacy policy (https://baseline.io/en/help/privacy-policy), which is what closes the gap. The old domain baselinetelematics.com serves the identical homepage and every internal link on it points to baseline.io, so baseline.io is the canonical home.
sells_why: Homepage sells municipal fleet and field operations: 'Dispatch & Fleet Ops ... real-time tracking, scheduling, and analytics', a SNOWMAN municipal snow-operations product, and usage-based 'Pay-as-you-Drive' insurance telematics since 2012 - i.e. fleet telematics and GPS, which is what we say they sell. The word 'telematics' never appears on the homepage, only in the legal pages.

name: IDI
quote: Transforming data into intelligence, IDI enables the real-time identification and location of people, businesses, assets and their interrelationships.
identity_why: identity_note: present ['idi'], missing [] but ok=false - identifies() can never pass a three-letter name (its 'strong' words must be over three characters), which is the short_name() case the repo routes to a person. What settles it here is not the three letters: og:site_name is 'IDI', the logo alt text is 'IDI-Logo a red violet company', and the product menu lists idiCORE, idiVERIFIED, idiTRACE, idiCRIM. Corroborated from the other direction: idicore.com redirects to login.idicore.com, whose support address is idicoresupport@ididata.com.
sells_why: Solutions lead with idiCORE, use cases include 'Investigations and Due Diligence' and 'Skip Tracing', industries include 'Government and Law Enforcement' - the IdiCORE investigative identity data platform we describe, and the reason it would exhibit at IACP.

name: Johnson Controls OpenBlue

identity_why: identity_note: ok=true, present ['johnson','controls','openblue'], missing [] - all three words of the company name are in the page's own title and description. The company here is a product line, so this is the product page rather than johnsoncontrols.com, whose title is only 'Johnson Controls' and would fail on 'openblue' the way aboutamazon.eu failed for AWS.
sells_why: The page is the OpenBlue smart-building platform - OpenBlue Companion/Employee/Visitor, building data unification, AI-driven insight - which is 'smart building operations software platform', our description.

name: Oracle NetSuite for Government
why: Nothing readable answered. add_company.fetch() on https://www.netsuite.com, https://www.netsuite.com/portal/industries/government.shtml and https://www.oracle.com/netsuite/ all returned HTTP 403; the same three through the repo's Playwright renderer (scripts/render_fetch.py's browser and UA) returned a 294-byte Akamai page titled 'Access Denied' ('You don't have permission to access ... on this server'), and oracle.com/netsuite/ redirects into netsuite.com/portal/home.shtml which is denied too. This is a refusal to this network, not evidence the site does not exist - it plainly does. I did not fall back to oracle.com, because the parent's homepage is the aboutamazon.eu mistake in a different suit: it would neither name NetSuite nor show the government ERP product.

name: PlayerU Software Solutions LLC
why: The name resolves, the business does not. playeru.com is a 114-byte parking redirect to /lander. playeru.ai is real: og:site_name 'PlayerU', title 'PlayerU - Your Pickleball Start', and press releases for 'PlayerU Software Solutions LLC' (Miami) point at that domain, so it is very likely the same legal entity. But the rendered site is a consumer pickleball-coaching app - 'PlayerU guides beginners step-by-step until they reach Court Ready status', App Store and Google Play buttons - and the words facility, league, program, reservation and booking do not appear anywhere on it. We say this company sells 'sports facility and program management software'. Identity passes, the product does not, so I am not writing the URL: somebody should reconcile the description first, then playeru.ai is the candidate to confirm.

name: SoilFLO
quote: SoilFLO is a digital load tracking software for construction and environmental teams to effectively manage materials like soil, C&D waste, aggregates, and haulage to better manage their earthworks projects or facilities.
identity_why: og:site_name is 'SoilFLO' and the title is 'SoilFLO - Material Tracking Software'. Two things had to be worked around. (1) add_company.fetch() gets HTTP 403/202 here - the site refuses the repo's crawler UA - so the page was read with the Playwright browser scripts/render_fetch.py already uses, and judged with find_websites afterwards. (2) On the real page identity_note still returns ok=false: PARKED matches the bare string 'sedo' inside the word 'onmousedown' in a WP Rocket script in the first 4KB, so a live company homepage is scored as a parked domain.
sells_why: Nav is Heavy Civil Contractors, Facilities, Earthworks Projects, plus an O. Reg 406/19 compliance guide - soil and excavated material tracking, our description.

name: Uber Technologies, Inc.

Domain is the exact brand name. www.uber.com answers HTTP 406 to the repo's crawler UA, so the homepage was read with the Playwright browser from scripts/render_fetch.py; https://www.uber.com/us/en/transit/ answers 200 to the ordinary fetcher and is titled 'Expand Your Services | Uber Transit'.
sells_why: The transit sub-site is the SLED half of the business we describe: 'Uber Transit ... Learn more about how we support transit agencies', with Vouchers, Central and APIs as the agency products - an on-demand mobility platform sold through agency partnerships.

quote: Virtual Project Manager has made both our inspectors and my jobs easier by providing a simple, web-based platform, to implement all our information in one location. - Ray Leftwich, City Engineer
